messages:
Lena: Noticed a p95 spike on redwood-13b-seq workloads after yesterday's runtime patch. Repro on canary; seems tied to torch.compile + cudagraph interactions.
Omar: Which sequence lengths / batch sizes? Any KV activity?
Lena: Mostly seqlen=768 and 1024, batch 1-2. KV cache hit ~95% for these tests. P95 went from ~34ms -> ~48ms.
Priya: Do you have an nsys breakdown? Kernel churn around token boundaries?
Lena: Yes, nsys shows a sharp switch at token 256 boundary: `attn_fused_opt` drops and `attn_fallback_v1` dominates. Simple table in trace: 
```
SEQLEN RANGE    attn_fused_opt   attn_fallback_v1   other
0..256          88%              6%                 6%
256..1024       18%              72%                10%
```
Omar: That smells like graph capture occurring with a short prefix, then later reuse sees different KV/non-empty state and kernel selector chooses the generic fallback. torch.compile + cudagraph can freeze an initial shape/memory layout.
Priya: Could also be that cudagraph capture uses different alloc offsets when KV goes from empty->populated, so memory stride heuristics flip.
bench-bot: perf snapshot: https://perf.internal/snapshots/2135802468 (baseline vs canary) attached.
Lena: Quick test: set RUNTIME_CUDAGRAPH=0 and the p95 returns to ~36ms. So capture path is implicated.
Omar: Short-term: force the fused kernel on dynamic paths when seqlen >= X, or disable cudagraph for kvcache-heavy requests. Also consider adding a capture-mode tag to autotuner keys.
Priya: Agree. Long-term: autotuner needs to include capture-mode and kvcache occupancy in its profiling grid. Right now it profiles (arch, seqlen, batch) only.
Lena: I'm opening a small runtime flag PR to opt-out of cudagraph when kv-mismatch detected at runtime. Will also add telemetry that logs kernel_selector decisions during captures.
Priya: We should also add a cheap microbenchmark at capture time that probes whether fused kernels are still valid under current kv layout. If it fails, skip capture reuse.
Omar: Implementation note: doing a microprobe per capture adds ~1ms overhead, but only on first warm token—seems worth it.
Lena: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4892 includes `runtime.capture_kv_probe` flag + telemetry. Marked as hotfix.
bench-bot: autotune job queued: autotune-capture-context-2135802468 (ETA ~30m).
Priya: Also, can we dump `kernel_proposals.json` from the autotuner on the canary? I want to compare proposals when capture-mode=on vs off.
Omar: I'll run repro with the script: `./tools/repro.sh --model redwood-13b --seqs 128,256,768,1024 --kv on --capture on,off` and attach traces + kernel proposals.
Lena: Tagging @eng-releases: please hold further rollouts of the runtime until we validate the canary with the capture probe enabled.
eng-releases: Acknowledged. We'll pause the global rollout and only allow the canary with PR flag enabled.
Priya: One more observation from NVTXs: cudagraph span begins before kvcache handshake completes for some codepaths. If capture encloses an incomplete handshake, the captured kernel layout may be invalid for subsequent tokens.
Omar: Good catch. Fixing handshake ordering or ensuring capture only after KV stabilization might be cleaner than blanket disabling. Add to ticket.
Lena: I'll open the ticket with repro steps, traces, and the PR link. Please drop any microbench outputs into that ticket.
bench-bot: Ticket created: https://tickets.internal/RT-13258 - autotune + capture kernel flip.
Lena: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the autotune outputs when job completes. If anyone sees the same regression on other models, ping here and attach traces.
